chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: He narrated to me Sulayman ibn Haf al-Marwazi, who said: I heard him saying:

When the fasting person rinses his mouth in the month of Ramadan, or inhales deliberately, or smells a strong scent, or sweeps a house and dust enters his nose and throat, then upon him is the fasting of two consecutive months, for that is considered breaking his fast for him, like eating, drinking, and intercourse.

The correct interpretation of this report is that we construe it regarding one who rinsed for cooling, something entered his throat, he did not spit it out, and swallowed it deliberately; then the ruling upon him is the same as the ruling upon one who deliberately broke his fast for one day of Ramadan.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a fasting person swallowing dust or water while rinsing their mouth in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the distinction between minor and major breaking of the fast by attributing the severe expiation (kaffarah) of two consecutive months to deliberate swallowing of dust or water, akin to eating or drinking. The concluding analysis suggests this ruling specifically applies to those who rinse for cooling and fail to spit out the residue, thereby linking the physical act to the intentionality required for major iftar.
